reference_items.stem:
The figure represents two similar triangles. The triangles are not drawn to scale.

In the actual triangle ABC, what is the length of side BC?
reference_items.figure_description:
Two right triangles are shown side by side:
- On the left is triangle ABC: vertical leg AB on the left, horizontal base BC on the bottom, with vertex B at the right-angle corner. Hypotenuse AC is labeled "6 cm". Inside angle A is labeled "50°" and inside angle C is labeled "40°".
- On the right is a larger triangle DEF: vertical leg DE on the left, horizontal base EF on the bottom labeled "15 cm", with vertex E at the right-angle corner. Hypotenuse DF is labeled "20 cm". Inside angle D is labeled "50°" and inside angle F is labeled "40°".

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it.
